analysis:
This PR changes only documentation in docs/provider/cli-reference.md, in the `darkbloom status` Traffic bullet (base lines 1045-1052, head 1045-1062). It adds the following to the docs: Traffic is judged from current evidence only; a `received a coordinator request … ago` eligibility path (state field `coordinator_connection.last_request_at`); a `not yet eligible` state for the first 90 seconds (`statusGraceSeconds`); a refusal reason shown for 60 seconds (`refusalMaxAge`); and the statement that the provider re-registers on the same verdict.

No code, key handling, protocol, or authorization logic is modified. The base text I could view (lines 805-1726) contains no security-control regression. The head side of the patch is truncated, so I cannot confirm the full new Traffic wording.

The doc says `eligible` may now be shown when the coordinator routed a request after its latest status. This is a local diagnostic, not an authorization decision. Coordinator-owned authorization remains the authority (A-016, T-052, T-053 in TB-011). Whether the provider code actually treats a received request as grounds to keep serving, or to re-register, is not in the supplied evidence. If it did, that could be a stale-authorization concern under T-053. That would need review of the provider implementation (StatusCommand+Traffic.swift, ServingReadiness.swift), which was not supplied; it is recorded here as an unverified contract, not a finding.

I did not see any new attack surface, data exposure, or invalidation of threat-model assumptions in the visible text. Messages shown to the operator carry coordinator-supplied reasons, which are rendered in the CLI; the docs do not indicate any sanitization concern.

The prefix-cache definition T-041 is unaffected by this change.
